result: {"stdout":"# HEIMDALL ROUTING — the pipeline from the moment a prompt is submitted

> **The Fold is the whole system (naming, 2026-10-01).** This map is the routing
> of its core, the khora (the eoreader7 repo). Around it: penelope (the keeper —
> the record · the mouth · the judgment, Mouth@1 on 11439), and the surfaces
> (where the hand comes back to the loom) — of which **the fold** (the holodeck
> repo, renamed) is the reading/research surface. The former `the-fold` repo is
> being absorbed by plane (generation → penelope, information-processing →
> eoreader7, surfacing → the fold/holodeck) and will be archived; where it still
> runs below, its servers are legacy. The mouth, the doors, and the seams this
> map describes are unchanged by the rename.

> **The mouth is Penelope's (2026-10-01).** The map below describes the
> reading engine and its doors — they stand. What changed: the mouth that
> the doors and the reading draw through is no longer eoreader7's. Penelope
> (`penelope/organs/mouth.mjs` + `penelope/mouth/server.mjs`, Mouth@1 on
> `PENELOPE_MOUTH_PORT` 11439) owns the decision — admission (the ration per
> identity, typed 429/503 + Retry-After), model choice, kind→wire routing —
> and directs the BRIDGE to execute: Heimdall's channel (11434), the
> AntiStrauss gate, the host picker, the upstream lanes. The engine draws
> through her at `native/kernel/mouth.js` (MOUTH_URL/MOUTH_IDENTITY); the
> proxy's in-process draws route through her generation door
> (`GENERATION_DOOR` → `organs/generation-door.mjs`). GL-RR-04 is the
> standing rule with its falsifying control. The one disclosed exception:
> when Penelope herself is unreachable, the proxy falls through to the
> direct host path, named (`draw_door_unreachable`), never silent.

A map of what happens inside eoreader7 (`/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/eoreader7`) as
soon as someone submits a prompt. Every claim descends to a real path:line.

The spine: **a prompt enters at a doorway → the swarm reads it before any model
load (hard meaning) → Heimdall admits or queues it (a typed 429, never a hang)
→ the turn DEFs a void and either asks the person back to fill it (the other
way prompting goes) or fills it itself → the model's draft races the mechanical
pipeline → the response rides out with the whole record disclosed.**

---

## 1. The doorways — where a prompt can enter

One process, two ports, one handler (`proxy.mjs:117–121`, `1662–1675`):
port 11436 (`ER7_PROXY_PORT`), and the heimdall alias port 11437
(`ER7_HEIMDALL_PORT`) so older clients that pointed at the standalone steer
still land on the same code.

| Doorway | Path | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Plain | `POST /v1/ask` `{task}` | no roles, no scaffolding (`proxy.mjs:648`) |
| OpenAI | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | `er7:`-prefixed models (`proxy.mjs:930`) |
| Ollama | `POST /api/chat` | ollama wire (`proxy.mjs:1269`) |
| Anthropic | `POST /v1/messages` | anthropic wire (`proxy.mjs:1480`) |
| Code | `POST /v1/code` | physics-gated loop (`proxy.mjs:788`) |
| Agent | `POST /v1/agent` | sandboxed open coding loop (`proxy.mjs:859`) |
| Swarm | `POST /v1/swarm` | explicit capacity-swarm, `force: true` (`proxy.mjs:617`) |
| Documents | `POST /v1/documents` | detached essay job (`proxy.mjs:466`) |
| Surfaces | TUI (`cli/tui.mjs`), browser (`GET /ui`, `proxy.mjs:1610`), Fold | all talk through the same routes |

Identity rides headers, never the body: `x-er7-session` (one accumulating fold),
`x-er7-user` (durable person across sessions, `proxy.mjs:172–187`),
`x-er7-workspace`, `x-er7-mode` (`auto|chat|long|origami`, `proxy.mjs:212–216`).
The caller is read mechanically — doorway, user-agent, tools, transcript shape —
into an interlocutor belief (agent/person/unknown), Buber, never asked of the
model (`callerFromRequest`, `proxy.mjs:224–241`; `native/organs/interlocutor.js:65–105`).

# The pass: keeping the horses running across many servers

Written 2026-09-21 against `60b7337` after reading every line of `src/` and
the eoreader7 side (`eoreader7/heimdall.mjs`, `heimdall-fleet.mjs`,
`native/docs/HEIMDALL-FLEET.md`, the 2026-09-21 traffic-jam post-mortem).
Each claim below names the line it stands on. "Landed" means shipped in this
pass; "next" is ordered, and each item states the control that would prove
it wrong.

## What "a horse" is, and who keeps it running

A horse is one device that accepted duty: a browser tab holding a WebLLM
model, reached over a WebRTC DataChannel whose offer/answer/ICE rode Matrix
to-device events. The room is a directory only (`src/matrix.js` header). The
controller — one browser tab — is the only thing that keeps a horse linked:
`reconcile()` every 15 s offers a link to every device of every member
(`main.js` `reconcile`), the worker pings every 15 s
(`acceptDuty` interval), and the lease is 12 h by the worker's own hand.

## Why it was "OK, not great" — the five holes, and what landed

1. **Silence was invisible.** The controller only learned a horse was gone
   when the DataChannel closed (`ensureWorkerLink` `onClose`). A suspended
   phone, a sleeping laptop, a NAT that dropped the path — the channel lingers
   for minutes, the list read *ready*, and the router (`route.js`
   `isEligible`) kept sending it work that timed out at 120 s.
   **Landed:** `src/liveness.js`. Standing is derived from the last ping,
   never the channel: ready → stale (3 missed pings, shown, not routable) →
   dead (6 missed, link torn down and re-offered). `isEligible` consults it.
   (The `liveness.test.mjs` once cited here does not exist in the tree;
   liveness is untested by the automated suite — see ACTIVITIES.md.) The bound the-fold already
   proved for its own mouths — "never convict on absence alone" — is kept:
   a record never heard from is *linking*, not dead.

2. **A horse that came back was ignored.** The worker re-announces `ready`
   every 20 s, but the controller's handler only called `reconcile()`, which
   skips any key already in `app.workers` — so a stale record blocked the
   relink forever. **Landed:** a `ready` from a device whose record is not
   ready/linking drops the husk and re-offers.

3. **Two reconcile loops.** `createRoom` and `rejoin` each started their own
   `setInterval`; a page that did both offered every horse twice as often.
   **Landed:** `startReconcile()`, one loop per page.

4. **The close-timer could reap a relinked horse.** `onClose` deleted by key
   after 5 s, even if a new record already sat under that key.
   **Landed:** it now reaps only its own record.

5. **The model pin compared against the picker, not the weights.**
   `onWorkerRtcMessage` refused on `app.modelId` (the `<select>`) while the
   hello/ping reported `engine.modelId`. **Landed:** both read the engine.

## Removing a device via Matrix (landed)

There was no way to remove a horse. A kicked worker would also have kept its
`heimdall.verified.<room>` flag and skipped the pairing proof on return — and
the controller linked every room member regardless of pairing, so the proof
only ever gated the worker's own willingness.

result: {"stdout":"# ACTIVITIES — everything heimdall does, and what happens when it breaks

Written 2026-10-04 against the current tree, after reading every file in
`src/` and running the whole test suite. Every activity below descends to a
real path; where a claim is unproven it is marked, never dressed up. The
project's own rule: a "wired" claim is checked against the code, and a
feature with no test and no live traffic is reported as wired-but-unproven.

## The one law: degradation, not failure

Heimdall's work nests in layers, and each layer's job is either **possibility**
(the layer always exists, no matter what breaks above it) or **probability**
(the layer makes the good path the usual path). A higher layer that breaks
never kills the work: the request **steps down** to the next layer that can
serve it, and the record shows the drop. The work continues, just not as well.

The ladder, by power, then by fallback:

```
1  frontier   a sealed external provider (groq/anthropic/openai/…)   probability
2  native     a linked native app host (LAN/Tailscale, real GPU)     probability
3  fleet      browser-tab horses (WebLLM/WebGPU + WASM fallback)     probability
4  upstream   this machine's own Ollama (the guaranteed floor)       possibility
5  in-tab     the page's own WebLLM when the bridge is gone         possibility
```

`runOnGiver` (`src/bridge-server.mjs`) walks rungs 1→3 in order: a rung that
fails **before its first token** steps down to the next; a rung that dies
mid-stream never steps down (the caller already holds partial output). When
the ladder is exhausted the bridge's callers answer from rung 4 (`upstream`).
The drop is never silent: `stats.fellThrough` counts it once per request, and
when a lower rung inside the ladder serves, the dispatch ledger records
`reason: "fell-through"` with the lane that **actually** served — so the
meter's "exact external tokens" can never be inflated by a frontier that
failed.

## The layers, what each does, and its test truth

### L1 — The doors (heimdall as a part of The Fold)

The wire shapes the surfaces speak; heimdall executes none of them:

| Door | Route | Goes to | Live |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama wire | `POST /api/chat`, `/api/generate` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| OpenAI wire | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Anthropic wire | `POST /v1/messages` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Machine door | `POST /api/code` | a local `opencode serve` (`src/opencode-lane.js`) | configured, idle |
| Read door | `POST /api/read` | the khora's model-free reader | configured, live seam |
| Generation door | `POST /api/weave` | penelope's weave | configured, no consumer yet |
| Keys | `POST /api/providers/keys` | `~/.heimdall/state.json` (loopback socket check) | yes (tested) |
| Links | `/link/*` | `~/.heimdall/hosts.json` | yes (untested at the bridge) |
| Controller | `/bridge/events`, `/bridge/state`, `/bridge/reply` | the open SSE controller tab | wired, unauthenticated |
| Accounting | `/api/ledger`, `/api/meter`, `/api/frontier`, `/status` | the dispatch ledger + stats | yes (tested) |

### L2 — The gate (admission)

Who and what may cross, before any routing:

- **Loopback bind** — the bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 (`src/bridge-server.mjs`).
- **Origin wall** — a request with an `Origin` header is refused unless it is
  the bridge's own page, any loopback page, or an explicit `allowedOrigins` /
  `HEIMDALL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` entry. Never `*`.
- **The sealed frontier gate** — a frontier model is reached only when the
  body carries `heimdall_privacy: "sealed-external"` (the Fold's privacy
  mode). This is the Fold's trust boundary for outside models.
  **Honest limit:** the label is caller-asserted — the gate cannot tell
  whether the bytes under it really are a sealed projection. It stops
  accidents, not a malicious caller.

Short answer: the horses aren't running because nothing is controlling them. I found two causes, one operational and one structural. I haven't changed any code.

I read "the scores.patch.points version" as the canonical repo at `3.0/heimdall` (origin `scores-patch-points/heimdall`). Tell me if you meant something else.

**What the live instance shows**

The `heimdall up` process (pid 65098, port 8790) reports this from `/status`:

```
tab:false  room:null  workers:[]  stats:{fleet:0, passthrough:481, frontier:319, code:63}
```

- **No controller, no horses.** A "horse" is a browser tab running WebLLM. Only a controller tab can link horses over Matrix and WebRTC, and only `reconcile()` in [main.js](../heimdall/src/main.js) keeps them linked. This instance was started with `--no-open`, so no controller tab exists and the room was never created. Every request has gone to Ollama or the frontier providers. The fleet has served nothing.
- **Horses depend on one open tab.** The controller is a single browser page, as the CLI says: "keep the page open — it is the fleet's controller." If that tab sleeps, closes or is throttled, every horse loses its keeper.
- **The headless controller was never built.** [MULTI-SERVER.md](../heimdall/MULTI-SERVER.md) calls this "Next 2" and says there is "no always-on process; horses die at the tab's sleep." The bridge's auto-reopen only tries to reopen the tab, and `--no-open` turns that off.
- **Unattended horses stop at 12 hours.** The lease is renewed by hand by design, and the auto-renew fix is still marked "owed."

**Why this went unnoticed**

- **No liveness test exists.** The stale/dead logic in [liveness.js](../heimdall/src/liveness.js) has no test, even though the doc says it does. ACTIVITIES.md also lists the browser-tab horses as "no automated test" and "no horses live."
- **The unit tests pass.** `node --test src/*.test.mjs` gave 297 passing, 0 failing, 1 cancelled. The cancelled one is `capsule-attack.test.mjs`, which hung for 88 seconds. None of the passing tests cover keeping horses alive.
- **The canonical repo dropped its tests.** Its first commit says "No tests, no dist, no node_modules", so a regression in horse-keeping could land with nothing to catch it.

**What I'd do, in order**

1. **Quick, today:** restart `heimdall up` without `--no-open` and keep the tab open. That gets horses linking again, but it doesn't make them durable.
2. **Real fix:** extract the controller from `main.js` into a `src/controller.js`, run it inside the `up` process with `node-datachannel`, and add a test where the controller tab dies and the horses relink within 90 seconds. This is the largest piece of work.
3. **Auto-renew:** add the opt-in lease auto-renew. It changes the consent design the README states, so it's your call.

Which do you want: the quick restart, or the headless controller? If you meant a different problem, such as horses dropping while a tab is open, tell me and I'll investigate that instead.

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/ACTIVITIES.md","content":"# ACTIVITIES — everything heimdall does, and what happens when it breaks

Written 2026-10-04 against the current tree, after reading every file in
`src/` and running the whole test suite. Every activity below descends to a
real path; where a claim is unproven it is marked, never dressed up. The
project's own rule: a "wired" claim is checked against the code, and a
feature with no test and no live traffic is reported as wired-but-unproven.

## The one law: degradation, not failure

Heimdall's work nests in layers, and each layer's job is either **possibility**
(the layer always exists, no matter what breaks above it) or **probability**
(the layer makes the good path the usual path). A higher layer that breaks
never kills the work: the request **steps down** to the next layer that can
serve it, and the record shows the drop. The work continues, just not as well.

The ladder, by power, then by fallback:

```
1  frontier   a sealed external provider (groq/anthropic/openai/…)   probability
2  native     a linked native app host (LAN/Tailscale, real GPU)     probability
3  fleet      browser-tab horses (WebLLM/WebGPU + WASM fallback)     probability
4  upstream   this machine's own Ollama (the guaranteed floor)       possibility
5  in-tab     the page's own WebLLM when the bridge is gone         possibility
```

`runOnGiver` (`src/bridge-server.mjs`) walks rungs 1→3 in order: a rung that
fails **before its first token** steps down to the next; a rung that dies
mid-stream never steps down (the caller already holds partial output). When
the ladder is exhausted the bridge's callers answer from rung 4 (`upstream`).
The drop is never silent: `stats.fellThrough` counts it once per request, and
when a lower rung inside the ladder serves, the dispatch ledger records
`reason: "fell-through"` with the lane that **actually** served — so the
meter's "exact external tokens" can never be inflated by a frontier that
failed.

## The layers, what each does, and its test truth

### L1 — The doors (heimdall as a part of The Fold)

The wire shapes the surfaces speak; heimdall executes none of them:

| Door | Route | Goes to | Live |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama wire | `POST /api/chat`, `/api/generate` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| OpenAI wire | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Anthropic wire | `POST /v1/messages` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Machine door | `POST /api/code` | a local `opencode serve` (`src/opencode-lane.js`) | configured, idle |
| Read door | `POST /api/read` | the khora's model-free reader | configured, live seam |
| Generation door | `POST /api/weave` | penelope's weave | configured, no consumer yet |
| Keys | `POST /api/providers/keys` | `~/.heimdall/state.json` (loopback socket check) | yes (tested) |
| Links | `/link/*` | `~/.heimdall/hosts.json` | yes (untested at the bridge) |
| Controller | `/bridge/events`, `/bridge/state`, `/bridge/reply` | the open SSE controller tab | wired, unauthenticated |
| Accounting | `/api/ledger`, `/api/meter`, `/api/frontier`, `/status` | the dispatch ledger + stats | yes (tested) |

### L2 — The gate (admission)

Who and what may cross, before any routing:

- **Loopback bind** — the bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 (`src/bridge-server.mjs`).
- **Origin wall** — a request with an `Origin` header is refused unless it is
  the bridge's own page, any loopback page, or an explicit `allowedOrigins` /
  `HEIMDALL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` entry. Never `*`.
- **The sealed frontier gate** — a frontier model is reached only when the
  body carries `heimdall_privacy: "sealed-external"` (the Fold's privacy
  mode). This is the Fold's trust boundary for outside models.

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/MULTI-SERVER.md","content":"# The pass: keeping the horses running across many servers

Written 2026-09-21 against `60b7337` after reading every line of `src/` and
the eoreader7 side (`eoreader7/heimdall.mjs`, `heimdall-fleet.mjs`,
`native/docs/HEIMDALL-FLEET.md`, the 2026-09-21 traffic-jam post-mortem).
Each claim below names the line it stands on. "Landed" means shipped in this
pass; "next" is ordered, and each item states the control that would prove
it wrong.

## What "a horse" is, and who keeps it running

A horse is one device that accepted duty: a browser tab holding a WebLLM
model, reached over a WebRTC DataChannel whose offer/answer/ICE rode Matrix
to-device events. The room is a directory only (`src/matrix.js` header). The
controller — one browser tab — is the only thing that keeps a horse linked:
`reconcile()` every 15 s offers a link to every device of every member
(`main.js` `reconcile`), the worker pings every 15 s
(`acceptDuty` interval), and the lease is 12 h by the worker's own hand.

## Why it was "OK, not great" — the five holes, and what landed

1. **Silence was invisible.** The controller only learned a horse was gone
   when the DataChannel closed (`ensureWorkerLink` `onClose`). A suspended
   phone, a sleeping laptop, a NAT that dropped the path — the channel lingers
   for minutes, the list read *ready*, and the router (`route.js`
   `isEligible`) kept sending it work that timed out at 120 s.
   **Landed:** `src/liveness.js`. Standing is derived from the last ping,
   never the channel: ready → stale (3 missed pings, shown, not routable) →
   dead (6 missed, link torn down and re-offered). `isEligible` consults it.
   (The `liveness.test.mjs` once cited here does not exist in the tree;
   liveness is untested by the automated suite — see ACTIVITIES.md.) The bound the-fold already
   proved for its own mouths — "never convict on absence alone" — is kept:
   a record never heard from is *linking*, not dead.

2. **A horse that came back was ignored.** The worker re-announces `ready`
   every 20 s, but the controller's handler only called `reconcile()`, which
   skips any key already in `app.workers` — so a stale record blocked the
   relink forever. **Landed:** a `ready` from a device whose record is not
   ready/linking drops the husk and re-offers.

3. **Two reconcile loops.** `createRoom` and `rejoin` each started their own
   `setInterval`; a page that did both offered every horse twice as often.
   **Landed:** `startReconcile()`, one loop per page.

4. **The close-timer could reap a relinked horse.** `onClose` deleted by key
   after 5 s, even if a new record already sat under that key.
   **Landed:** it now reaps only its own record.

5. **The model pin compared against the picker, not the weights.**
   `onWorkerRtcMessage` refused on `app.modelId` (the `<select>`) while the
   hello/ping reported `engine.modelId`. **Landed:** both read the engine.

## Removing a device via Matrix (landed)

There was no way to remove a horse. A kicked worker would also have kept its
`heimdall.verified.<room>` flag and skipped the pairing proof on return — and
the controller linked every room member regardless of pairing, so the proof
only ever gated the worker's own willingness.

Removal is now three acts, each enforced by a different body
(`main.js` `removeWorker`):

| Act | Body that enforces it | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Room | the homeserver, for every surface | `kick` (leave now) or `ban` (out until unban) — `MatrixPeer.kick/ban/unban` |
| Account | every controller signed into the account | `org.heimdall.revoked` account data (`invite.js` `revokeDevice`); `reconcile` consults `isRevoked` before offering a link; the pairing is forgotten (`forgetPairedKey`) so a return must prove its code again |
| Link | the worker itself, at once | a `revoked` to-device notice + t… [6303 more chars at the transcript address]

Written 2026-10-04 against the current tree, after reading every file in
`src/` and running the whole test suite. Every activity below descends to a
real path; where a claim is unproven it is marked, never dressed up. The
project's own rule: a "wired" claim is checked against the code, and a
feature with no test and no live traffic is reported as wired-but-unproven.

## The one law: degradation, not failure

Heimdall's work nests in layers, and each layer's job is either **possibility**
(the layer always exists, no matter what breaks above it) or **probability**
(the layer makes the good path the usual path). A higher layer that breaks
never kills the work: the request **steps down** to the next layer that can
serve it, and the record shows the drop. The work continues, just not as well.

The ladder, by power, then by fallback:

```
1  frontier   a sealed external provider (groq/anthropic/openai/…)   probability
2  native     a linked native app host (LAN/Tailscale, real GPU)     probability
3  fleet      browser-tab horses (WebLLM/WebGPU + WASM fallback)     probability
4  upstream   this machine's own Ollama (the guaranteed floor)       possibility
5  in-tab     the page's own WebLLM when the bridge is gone         possibility
```

`runOnGiver` (`src/bridge-server.mjs`) walks rungs 1→3 in order: a rung that
fails **before its first token** steps down to the next; a rung that dies
mid-stream never steps down (the caller already holds partial output). When
the ladder is exhausted the bridge's callers answer from rung 4 (`upstream`).
The drop is never silent: `stats.fellThrough` counts it once per request, and
when a lower rung inside the ladder serves, the dispatch ledger records
`reason: "fell-through"` with the lane that **actually** served — so the
meter's "exact external tokens" can never be inflated by a frontier that
failed.

## The layers, what each does, and its test truth

### L1 — The doors (heimdall as a part of The Fold)

The wire shapes the surfaces speak; heimdall executes none of them:

| Door | Route | Goes to | Live |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama wire | `POST /api/chat`, `/api/generate` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| OpenAI wire | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Anthropic wire | `POST /v1/messages` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Machine door | `POST /api/code` | a local `opencode serve` (`src/opencode-lane.js`) | configured, idle |
| Read door | `POST /api/read` | the khora's model-free reader | configured, live seam |
| Generation door | `POST /api/weave` | penelope's weave | configured, no consumer yet |
| Keys | `POST /api/providers/keys` | `~/.heimdall/state.json` (loopback socket check) | yes (tested) |
| Links | `/link/*` | `~/.heimdall/hosts.json` | yes (untested at the bridge) |
| Controller | `/bridge/events`, `/bridge/state`, `/bridge/reply` | the open SSE controller tab | wired, unauthenticated |
| Accounting | `/api/ledger`, `/api/meter`, `/api/frontier`, `/status` | the dispatch ledger + stats | yes (tested) |

### L2 — The gate (admission)

Who and what may cross, before any routing:

- **Loopback bind** — the bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 (`src/bridge-server.mjs`).
- **Origin wall** — a request with an `Origin` header is refused unless it is
  the bridge's own page, any loopback page, or an explicit `allowedOrigins` /
  `HEIMDALL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` entry. Never `*`.
- **The sealed frontier gate** — a frontier model is reached only when the
  body carries `heimdall_privacy: "sealed-external"` (the Fold's privacy
  mode). This is the Fold's trust boundary for outside models.
  **Honest limit:** the label is caller-asserted — the gate cannot tell
  whether the bytes under it really are a sealed projection. … [5521 more chars at the transcript address]

```
1  frontier   a sealed external provider (groq/anthropic/openai/…)   probability
2  native     a linked native app host (LAN/Tailscale, real GPU)     probability
3  fleet      browser-tab horses (WebLLM/WebGPU + WASM fallback)     probability
4  upstream   this machine's own Ollama (the guaranteed floor)       possibility
5  in-tab     the page's own WebLLM when the bridge is gone         possibility
```

`runOnGiver` (`src/bridge-server.mjs`) walks rungs 1→3 in order: a rung that
fails **before its first token** steps down to the next; a rung that dies
mid-stream never steps down (the caller already holds partial output). When
the ladder is exhausted the bridge's callers answer from rung 4 (`upstream`).
The drop is never silent: `stats.fellThrough` counts it once per request, and
when a lower rung inside the ladder serves, the dispatch ledger records
`reason: "fell-through"` with the lane that **actually** served — so the
meter's "exact external tokens" can never be inflated by a frontier that
failed.

## The layers, what each does, and its test truth

### L1 — The doors (heimdall as a part of The Fold)

The wire shapes the surfaces speak; heimdall executes none of them:

| Door | Route | Goes to | Live |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama wire | `POST /api/chat`, `/api/generate` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| OpenAI wire | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Anthropic wire | `POST /v1/messages` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |
| Machine door | `POST /api/code` | a local `opencode serve` (`src/opencode-lane.js`) | configured, idle |
| Read door | `POST /api/read` | the khora's model-free reader | configured, live seam |
| Generation door | `POST /api/weave` | penelope's weave | configured, no consumer yet |
| Keys | `POST /api/providers/keys` | `~/.heimdall/state.json` (loopback socket check) | yes (tested) |
| Links | `/link/*` | `~/.heimdall/hosts.json` | yes (untested at the bridge) |
| Controller | `/bridge/events`, `/bridge/state`, `/bridge/reply` | the open SSE controller tab | wired, unauthenticated |
| Accounting | `/api/ledger`, `/api/meter`, `/api/frontier`, `/status` | the dispatch ledger + stats | yes (tested) |

### L2 — The gate (admission)

Who and what may cross, before any routing:

- **Loopback bind** — the bridge listens on 127.0.0.1 (`src/bridge-server.mjs`).
- **Origin wall** — a request with an `Origin` header is refused unless it is
  the bridge's own page, any loopback page, or an explicit `allowedOrigins` /
  `HEIMDALL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` entry. Never `*`.
- **The sealed frontier gate** — a frontier model is reached only when the
  body carries `heimdall_privacy: "sealed-external"` (the Fold's privacy
  mode). This is the Fold's trust boundary for outside models.
  **Honest limit:** the label is caller-asserted — the gate cannot tell
  whether the bytes under it really are a sealed projection. … [5521 more chars at the transcript address]

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/MULTI-SERVER.md","content":"# The pass: keeping the horses running across many servers

Written 2026-09-21 against `60b7337` after reading every line of `src/` and
the eoreader7 side (`eoreader7/heimdall.mjs`, `heimdall-fleet.mjs`,
`native/docs/HEIMDALL-FLEET.md`, the 2026-09-21 traffic-jam post-mortem).
Each claim below names the line it stands on. "Landed" means shipped in this
pass; "next" is ordered, and each item states the control that would prove
it wrong.

## What "a horse" is, and who keeps it running

A horse is one device that accepted duty: a browser tab holding a WebLLM
model, reached over a WebRTC DataChannel whose offer/answer/ICE rode Matrix
to-device events. The room is a directory only (`src/matrix.js` header). The
controller — one browser tab — is the only thing that keeps a horse linked:
`reconcile()` every 15 s offers a link to every device of every member
(`main.js` `reconcile`), the worker pings every 15 s
(`acceptDuty` interval), and the lease is 12 h by the worker's own hand.

## Why it was "OK, not great" — the five holes, and what landed

1. **Silence was invisible.** The controller only learned a horse was gone
   when the DataChannel closed (`ensureWorkerLink` `onClose`). A suspended
   phone, a sleeping laptop, a NAT that dropped the path — the channel lingers
   for minutes, the list read *ready*, and the router (`route.js`
   `isEligible`) kept sending it work that timed out at 120 s.
   **Landed:** `src/liveness.js`. Standing is derived from the last ping,
   never the channel: ready → stale (3 missed pings, shown, not routable) →
   dead (6 missed, link torn down and re-offered). `isEligible` consults it.
   (The `liveness.test.mjs` once cited here does not exist in the tree;
   liveness is untested by the automated suite — see ACTIVITIES.md.) The bound the-fold already
   proved for its own mouths — "never convict on absence alone" — is kept:
   a record never heard from is *linking*, not dead.

2. **A horse that came back was ignored.** The worker re-announces `ready`
   every 20 s, but the controller's handler only called `reconcile()`, which
   skips any key already in `app.workers` — so a stale record blocked the
   relink forever. **Landed:** a `ready` from a device whose record is not
   ready/linking drops the husk and re-offers.

3. **Two reconcile loops.** `createRoom` and `rejoin` each started their own
   `setInterval`; a page that did both offered every horse twice as often.
   **Landed:** `startReconcile()`, one loop per page.

4. **The close-timer could reap a relinked horse.** `onClose` deleted by key
   after 5 s, even if a new record already sat under that key.
   **Landed:** it now reaps only its own record.

5. **The model pin compared against the picker, not the weights.**
   `onWorkerRtcMessage` refused on `app.modelId` (the `<select>`) while the
   hello/ping reported `engine.modelId`. **Landed:** both read the engine.

## Removing a device via Matrix (landed)

There was no way to remove a horse. A kicked worker would also have kept its
`heimdall.verified.<room>` flag and skipped the pairing proof on return — and
the controller linked every room member regardless of pairing, so the proof
only ever gated the worker's own willingness.

Removal is now three acts, each enforced by a different body
(`main.js` `removeWorker`):

| Act | Body that enforces it | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Room | the homeserver, for every surface | `kick` (leave now) or `ban` (out until unban) — `MatrixPeer.kick/ban/unban` |
| Account | every controller signed into the account | `org.heimdall.revoked` account data (`invite.js` `revokeDevice`); `reconcile` consults `isRevoked` before offering a link; the pairing is forgotten (`forgetPairedKey`) so a return must prove its code again |
| Link | the worker itself, at once | a `revoked` to-device notice + t… [6303 more chars at the transcript address]

It prints a port map but does not start the bridge, the mouth or ollama, and nothing supervises the proxy either. The canonical port doc is `khora/docs/PORTS.md`.

  - fold-stack/lib/ollama.mjs:3 uses 11434.
  - the-fold/.claude/worktrees/agent-a793253b61ec96193 is a stale copy that still references 8790. Ignore it.

    - `com.fold.mouth`: `cd penelope && node mouth/server.mjs`
    - `com.fold.bridge`: `cd heimdall && node bin/heimdall.mjs up --no-open`. Add `ThrottleInterval=5`. launchd will respawn it, and the existing pidfile lock is harmless because it just exits 1 when a live pid holds it.

  - `floor.sh restart bridge` does `launchctl kickstart -k`, which is the clean way to load the uncommitted heimdall edits. Add `floor.sh status`, which prints each port's pid and start time against the repo's last-commit and file mtimes, to flag stale code.

input: {"message":"AUDIT: RUNG 1 (frontier) + RUNG 2 (native links) + the ladder router. Read-only. M = measured live or by a harmless script. I = inferred from reading code.

WHAT EACH RUNG DOES TODAY
- Rung 1, live bridge (pid 65098, started 03:47Z), M: GET /api/frontier returns `configured:false, providers:[]`. `/api/providers/keys` shows only an anthropic key stored. The last frontier dispatch was 18:27:59Z. Stats show frontier 319 and frontierRefused 0, and neither moved after that.
  - In the frontier-serving period: 186 sonnet-4-6 and 3 pollinations dispatches, all accepted. Median 15 s, max 157 s.
  - A fresh discovery script (default fetch) sees 4 anthropic models reachable (sonnet-5-5, opus-5-5, fable-5-1, ...). So the key works, but the live frontierMap is empty. The log shows "provider key stored for anthropic (0 model(s) reachable)" at 18:27:43 and again at 19:32:11. After either one the map held no frontier models.
- Rung 2, M: `/link/hosts` returns `{"links":[]}`, `~/.heimdall/hosts.json` does not exist, and stats.native is 0. It has never served anything.
- Rung 3 (fleet), M: `workers:[]`, `tab:false`. Every fleet attempt fails instantly with "no controller tab".
- The /api/meter and /api/ledger endpoints exist. Meter: frontier 319, externalTokens 68712.
- The live process runs older code than the working tree, I. Its log format ("key stored ... (server-side; N model(s) reachable)") does not exist in the current src/bridge-server.mjs.

WHY 13 FELL THROUGH (M, from /private/tmp/heimdall.log; the dispatch ledger holds none of them)
The 26 "failed before the first token" lines are 13 requests, each frontier then fleet ("no controller tab") then upstream Ollama.
- 9 were 401 "Missing API key" from the keyless llm7 proxy (llm7:*, and bare anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gemini-3-flash, gpt-oss:20b). Discovery marked them reachable and keyless.
- 4 were Anthropic 400 "`temperature` is deprecated for this model" on claude-sonnet-5 / claude-sonnet-5-5.
- None was a 429 or a timeout.

STEP-DOWN CONTRACT
- 20/20 pass in bridge-ladder.test.mjs and bridge-frontier.test.mjs.
- The live log confirms step-down works for thrown errors. The frontier lane served 3 pollinations dispatches.

DEFECTS, in importance order

1. A 429 or 5xx from a frontier provider counts as success with an empty answer (src/remote.js:48-49, 108-109, 189-190).
   - chatOpenAI, chatOllama and chatAnthropic return `{text:"", tokens:0, status:429|5xx}` instead of throwing with `beforeFirstToken`.
   - runOnFrontier (src/bridge-server.mjs:542) then logs a dispatch with 0 tokens and returns. runOnGiver (:497) never steps down. The caller sends an empty 200 "stop".
   - Reproduced with a fake fetch: `inferOn({provider:"anthropic",...},{fetchImpl:()=>new Response("",{status:429})})` returns `{"text":"","tokens":0,"status":429}` with no throw.
   - The ladder tests cover only thrown errors, so they miss this.
   - Fix: in the bridge, treat `status>=429 && !tokens` as `{beforeFirstToken:true}`. Better, throw it in remote.js.

2. refreshFrontier clears the map even when discovery found nothing (src/bridge-server.mjs:244 `frontierMap.clear()`). It is called after a key store, retest or refresh.
   - This is the probable cause of the dead live frontier: a valid key plus a 0-reachable refresh empties it, with no fallback to the previous map. The mechanism is I; the empty state is M.
   - Fix: only swap the map when `n>0`, or keep the old executors that were reachable before.
   - Operator remedy, not run by me: POST /api/providers/refresh or restart on the current code.

3. There is no circuit breaker or health memory. The `throttled()` check at :192 only feeds dispatchCandidates and the 429s it reads are never produced by the ladder. runOnGiver (:497) retries every dead rung on every request.
   - M: the same 401 or 400 was re-tried 13 times.

title: /bb280456-4247-4237-b900-81c0bdd1cea5/t4
text:
Here is the diagnosis so far, covering only what's been measured. The other four audits are still running and will fill in the floor, fleet, frontier and gate layers.

**Why it's been sucking**

1. **Nothing keeps anything running.** Every service has ppid 1, meaning none has a supervising parent. There's no launchd agent, no cron, and no supervising script. The only restart script, `khora/local-up.sh`, starts the khora proxy alone. The bridge, mouth and channel stay down after a crash or reboot until someone notices. Only Ollama survives, because Ollama.app supervises itself.

2. **The bridge is running stale code.** It started Oct 4 22:47. About 693 uncommitted lines across 9 heimdall files, including 410 in `bridge-server.mjs`, were edited since and aren't loaded. Nobody can tell by looking: `/api/route-stats` just returns 404.

3. **The fleet has never run.** The live `/status` showed `tab:false room:null workers:[] fleet:0`. The bridge was started with `--no-open`, so the controller tab was never opened and no horse ever linked. If the tab does exist, one sleeping tab strands all the horses, and the lease expires after 12 hours regardless. Everything has been served by Ollama and the frontier providers, so "heimdall" has been a pass-through.

4. **The dependency chain is long and each hop is unsupervised.** The path is the-fold page → bridge on 8790 → khora channel on 11434 → Ollama on 11435. The channel on 11434 is khora's code, not heimdall's. It was restarted by hand at 14:06 today. Any one broken hop looks like "heimdall is broken."

5. **Some callers bypass the ladder.** `fold-chat-loaded.js:18` talks straight to 11434, so a bridge outage never shows there. Penelope also calls 11434 directly. The documented rule is that a failing higher rung steps down, but in practice there are several side doors around it.

6. **Nothing detects any of this.** The liveness logic has no test, and the canonical repo was created without its tests. A regression in horse-keeping can ship and nobody finds out until the fleet is empty.

**Root cause, in one line:** the design says a failed rung steps down, but no layer, from the process up to the fleet, is built to stay up. Possibility is the floor, and the floor is a hand-started process chain with no supervisor.

**Next:** when the floor, fleet, frontier and gate reports land, I'll fix in this order: supervise and restart the floor, then the headless controller, then the frontier circuit breakers and gate holes.

    - Any Origin-less caller, or a page on ANY loopback port, can set `toolCapable:true` and a `cwd`, and get opencode shell and file access.
    - Fix: the token from S1, and ignore the caller-supplied `toolCapable` flag.
  
  - **S4 Medium, the Origin wall allows every loopback port** (line 335). Any local web page can read and write everything, including `POST /link/host`. That route has an SSRF probe and no socket check, and a link can hijack a model name and capture prompts. Fix: allow only the bridge's own origin and the named allowlist, not the whole `localhost:*` regex.
  
  - **S5 Medium, stored XSS on `/link`** (`linkPage`, lines 584–640). `l.name` and `l.url` go unescaped into HTML and `innerHTML`; `name` comes straight from `b.name` on line 1081. Script on the bridge's own origin passes the Origin wall. Fix: escape in `linkPage`, and validate `name` and `url`.

  - **S9 Low, unbounded growth.**
    - There is no cap on SSE `tabs` or on concurrent jobs.
    - `codeArtifacts` (line 159) and `comp` cells grow forever. `/api/dispatch/observe` accepts arbitrary model strings, and unauthenticated writers can poison routing competence.

text:
Two more reports are in, and the gate audit is the serious one. I'm still waiting on the floor and fleet audits.

**Gate, doors and record**

The working tree boots, and all 55 bridge tests pass. These problems are unrelated to why the horses aren't running:

- **Any local process can take over the bridge.** The newest `/bridge/events` connection becomes the controller. In the audit's smoke test, a script with no Origin header read a prompt and forged the model's answer.
- **DNS rebinding works.** There's no Host check, so a rebound page can read `/api/audit`, which contains full outbound prompts, and the native-host keys.
- **`/api/code` gives shell and file access.** Any local caller can ask for it.
- **The working tree can't be committed on its own.** It depends on seven untracked modules, so committing only the modified files would crash the committed bridge on import.
- **The test suite writes into the real outbound ledger.** It adds fixture traffic to `~/.heimdall/outbound-ledger.ndjson` (114KB so far), and the same ledger holds your real traffic.
- **Smaller defects:** unbounded request bodies, a static-path traversal into a sibling directory, and stored XSS on `/link`.

**The causes now confirmed** (the first three are from these two reports; the last is my earlier finding):

1. Nothing supervises the stack, and the bridge runs stale code.
2. The frontier map is empty on the live bridge.
3. Failing rungs are retried on every request, with no memory of failures.
4. The fleet has never had a controller.

I'm waiting on the floor and fleet audits before starting fixes.

You own exclusively: src/main.js, src/rtc.js, src/invite.js, src/matrix.js, src/liveness.js, src/route.js, src/swarm.js, src/liveness.test.mjs (already written and passing - extend it) and new test files you add. Another agent owns src/bridge-server.mjs, remote.js, links.mjs, bin/heimdall.mjs - do not touch them. Read MULTI-SERVER.md and src/liveness.js first.

Fix these measured defects in the browser-tab controller (each: failing test first, then fix; extract the small pure logic you need to test into exported helpers rather than testing main.js's DOM; keep behaviour otherwise identical):
1. main.js ~362 and ~371: a `ready` from a hidden or expired horse makes standingOf return away/expired, so the controller drops a healthy link (defeats AWAY_HOLD; expired horses churn every ~20s; ignores jobInFlight). Only drop a husk that is genuinely dead/lost/linking-stuck, never away/expired/stale, and never one with a job in flight.
2. invite.js ~174 revokedList swallows read errors and returns [] so a failed read FAILS OPEN and main.js refreshRevoked's keep-last-list never fires; invite.js ~148-151 and ~162-164 can overwrite the paired registry from a failed read. Make a failed read throw (or return a distinguishable error) so callers keep the last list and never write back from a failed read. Test with a fake fetch.
3. main.js ~792: revocation gates only new offers; a horse already linked stays routed. A revoked horse must be dropped and unrouted at the next reconcile tick.
4. main.js ~547-580 and ~192-193: createRoom/rejoin failure has no retry so startReconcile never runs until reload, and app.matrix is set before start() succeeds. Retry with backoff (e.g. 2s..60s) and only publish app.matrix after start succeeds.
5. main.js ~1509: a broadcast marks inflight with no timer so a dead horse's inflight never clears, jobInFlight stays true forever and the tick never relinks it. Add an inflight deadline (the job timeout) that clears it.
6. liveness.js ~43 / route.js ~51: an absent or 0 leaseUntil counts as unlimited so a horse that has not accepted yet is sent jobs. Define the intended rule: a horse is routable only after it has said it accepted duty (hello with leaseUntil > 0), and lease is judged by remaining time reported by the worker rather than comparing the phone's absolute clock to the controller's (accept both fields, prefer a `leaseMs`/remaining form if present, otherwise absolute with a documented skew tolerance of 60s). Update the KNOWN GAP test in liveness.test.mjs to assert the new rule.
7. rtc.js ~55-65: `_announced` never resets, so after a transient ICE `disconnected` (reported as close) `opened` stays false and main.js ~901-913 reaps the link after 5s, losing in-flight jobs. Treat `disconnected` as recoverable: wait a grace (e.g. 8s) for `connected` again before announcing close; only `failed`/`closed` are immediate. Write the test with a fake RTCPeerConnection class injected via globalThis.
8. main.js ~786-799: reconcile fetches devicesOf serially for every joined member before the heard filter: bound it (parallel with a small concurrency cap and a per-call timeout, skip members not seen in N days).
9. Minor: app.timers pushed and never cleared (~912,935); setIntervals stack on every renew (~1709-1724).

Also ADD `useIndexedDB:false`-style Node support to src/matrix.js ONLY as an opt-in option on the crypto init (e.g. MatrixPeer.start({ memoryCrypto:true })), default unchanged for the browser (current matrix.js:109-111 throws in Node because indexedDB is null). Do not build the headless controller yet.

input: {"description":"Fix bridge: frontier and gate","prompt":"You are an IMPLEMENTER. Repo: /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall (canonical heimdall). It already has ~700 lines of uncommitted work from an earlier session in src/bridge-server.mjs, bin/heimdall.mjs, src/discovery.js, src/job.js, src/remote.js, src/opencode-lane.js: build ON TOP of it, never revert or discard it. Do NOT git commit, do NOT restart/kill any running process (a live bridge on 8790 stays untouched; smoke-test only on a free high port like 18790 with temp files, then kill only your own process). You own these files exclusively: src/bridge-server.mjs, src/remote.js, src/links.mjs, src/dispatch.js, src/discovery.js, bin/heimdall.mjs, and the test files bridge*.test.mjs, remote.test.mjs, plus new test files you add. Another agent edits src/main.js, rtc.js, invite.js, matrix.js, liveness.js, route.js - do not touch those.

Read ACTIVITIES.md first. Fix, in this order, with a failing test written first for each (red then green; tests must be hermetic: pass a temp `auditFile`, temp state/hosts files, fake fetch; never touch ~/.heimdall or the real Ollama):

FRONTIER (measured defects from a live audit):
1. src/remote.js chatOpenAI/chatOllama/chatAnthropic (~lines 48,108,189) return {text:"",tokens:0,status:429|5xx} instead of throwing; runOnFrontier (bridge-server.mjs ~:542) then logs an empty success and the ladder never steps down. Make a non-2xx from a provider throw an error with beforeFirstToken:true and the status, so runOnGiver steps down. Test: fake fetch 429 and 503 -> the request is served by the next rung, ledger shows the fall-through.
2. refreshFrontier (~:244) does frontierMap.clear() even when discovery found 0 reachable -> a valid key plus a transient failed probe empties the frontier (this is the live state: configured:false with a working key). Only swap the map when the new discovery is non-empty; otherwise keep the previous executors and mark them stale. Test it.
3. No circuit breaker: the same 401 (keyless llm7 proxy, discovery wrongly marks it reachable) and 400 (claude-sonnet-5/5-5 reject `temperature`, remote.js ~:178) were retried on every request. Add a per-executor `downUntil` cooldown (60s on 401/400/403 or 2+ consecutive failures; shorter on 429 honouring Retry-After) consulted by runOnGiver and dispatchCandidates; omit `temperature` for anthropic models that reject it (retry once without it on that specific 400 and remember). Do not mark a keyless provider reachable on a models listing alone if a one-token chat probe returns 401 (keep it cheap, only at refresh).
4. Record each failed rung in the dispatch ledger ({reason:"rung-failed", lane, error, status}) not only the serving fall-through; the ledger must stay bounded.
5. Meter input tokens: runOnFrontier hardcodes inputTokens:0 though out.usage exists (~:546); use it.
6. runOnLink (~:475) has no timeout: add a first-byte AbortSignal (10s default, configurable) and a lastFailAt skip window in links resolution (src/links.mjs resolveLink); frontier gets a 15s first-byte bound in addition to the total timeout.

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/ACTIVITIES.md","content":"# ACTIVITIES — everything heimdall does, and what happens when it breaks

Written 2026-10-04 against the current tree, after reading every file in
`src/` and running the whole test suite. Every activity below descends to a
real path; where a claim is unproven it is marked, never dressed up. The
project's own rule: a "wired" claim is checked against the code, and a
feature with no test and no live traffic is reported as wired-but-unproven.

## The one law: degradation, not failure

Heimdall's work nests in layers, and each layer's job is either **possibility**
(the layer always exists, no matter what breaks above it) or **probability**
(the layer makes the good path the usual path). A higher layer that breaks
never kills the work: the request **steps down** to the next layer that can
serve it, and the record shows the drop. The work continues, just not as well.

The ladder, by power, then by fallback:

```
1  frontier   a sealed external provider (groq/anthropic/openai/…)   probability
2  native     a linked native app host (LAN/Tailscale, real GPU)     probability
3  fleet      browser-tab horses (WebLLM/WebGPU + WASM fallback)     probability
4  upstream   this machine's own Ollama (the guaranteed floor)       possibility
5  in-tab     the page's own WebLLM when the bridge is gone         possibility
```

`runOnGiver` (`src/bridge-server.mjs`) walks rungs 1→3 in order: a rung that
fails **before its first token** steps down to the next; a rung that dies
mid-stream never steps down (the caller already holds partial output). When
the ladder is exhausted the bridge's callers answer from rung 4 (`upstream`).
The drop is never silent: `stats.fellThrough` counts it once per request, and
when a lower rung inside the ladder serves, the dispatch ledger records
`reason: "fell-through"` with the lane that **actually** served — so the
meter's "exact external tokens" can never be inflated by a frontier that
failed.

## The layers, what each does, and its test truth

### L1 — The doors (heimdall as a part of The Fold)

The wire shapes the surfaces speak; heimdall executes none of them:

| Door | Route | Goes to | Live |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama wire | `POST /api/chat`, `/api/generate` | the ladder → rung 4 | yes (tested) |

# The Fold — local-up.sh: the durable way to start the pipeline on THIS box.
#
#   ./local-up.sh          foreground (logs to proxy.log)
#   ./local-up.sh bg       background
#
# One model host by default (the native Ollama daemon on 11435). The fleet
# bridge is opt-in only (ER7_FLEET_URL); the channel holds 11434 on both
# loopback families and forwards to the daemon.
#
# Canonical port map: docs/PORTS.md (and printed below on every start).
#
# The three rules this box runs by:
#   1. local → the native daemon (127.0.0.1:11435) — the only required host.
#   2. No ER7_OLLAMA_HOSTS override beyond that: the fleet bridge is NOT added
#      unless ER7_FLEET_URL names it (the proxy then adds it as a standby).
#   3. The channel holds 11434; the daemon is private at 11435. Point plain
#      ollama clients at 11435 to skip the gate, at 11434 to walk through it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# ── canonical ports (override any with the matching env var) ────────────────
PROXY_PORT="${ER7_PROXY_PORT:-11436}"
CHANNEL_PORT="${ER7_CHANNEL_PORT:-11434}"
OLLAMA_PORT="${ER7_OLLAMA_PORT:-11435}"
MOUTH_PORT="${PENELOPE_MOUTH_PORT:-11439}"
FLEET_PORT="${ER7_HEIMDALL_FLEET_PORT:-11438}"
OPENCODE_PORT="${ER7_OPENCODE_PORT:-4096}"

export ER7_OLLAMA_HOSTS="local=http://127.0.0.1:${OLLAMA_PORT}"
export ER7_FLEET_URL="${ER7_FLEET_URL:-}"
export ER7_OPENCODE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:${OPENCODE_PORT}"

# If the external heimdall fleet is already watching, run the proxy as a thin
# sandbox under it (a wedged proxy can then never take its own watcher down).
if curl -s -m 1 "http://127.0.0.1:${FLEET_PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export ER7_EXTERNAL_HEIMDALL=1
fi

# The second lane (`opencode serve`) draws frontier models through the
# opencode server's own HTTP API, which is basic-auth protected. Discover the
# running server's credentials from its process env rather than hardcoding
# them; a box with no server simply offers no frontier ids.
if [ -z "${OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  OCPID="$(pgrep -f 'opencode serve' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
  if [ -n "${OCPID:-}" ]; then
    PW="$(ps eww -p "$OCPID" 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=//p' | head -1)"
    US="$(ps eww -p "$OCPID" 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME=//p' | head -1)"
    [ -n "$PW" ] && export OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD="$PW"
    [ -n "$US" ] && export OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME="$US"
  fi
fi

print_map() {
  cat <<EOF

The Fold pipeline
  proxy (OpenAI · Ollama · Anthropic)  http://127.0.0.1:${PROXY_PORT}/v1
  self-describing map                  http://127.0.0.1:${PROXY_PORT}/
  health                               http://127.0.0.1:${PROXY_PORT}/health
  model prefix                         fold:<real-model>   (er7: still accepted)
  ollama daemon (direct)               http://127.0.0.1:${OLLAMA_PORT}
  ollama channel (gated)               http://127.0.0.1:${CHANNEL_PORT}
  penelope mouth                       http://127.0.0.1:${MOUTH_PORT}
  heimdall fleet                       http://127.0.0.1:${FLEET_PORT}
  opencode server (second mouth)       http://127.0.0.1:${OPENCODE_PORT}
EOF
}

if curl -s -m 1 "http://127.0.0.1:${PROXY_PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "proxy already up on http://127.0.0.1:${PROXY_PORT}"
  print_map
  exit 0
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = "bg" ]; then
  nohup node proxy.mjs >> proxy.log 2>&1 &
  echo "proxy starting in background (pid $!), logging to proxy.log"

else

# heimdall

Distributed local inference. You get a link. Anyone who opens it and presses
**Accept** turns their phone or laptop into a compute node you manage
collectively. Their device downloads a small model, runs it locally in the
browser, and streams answers back to you.

> **The whole map:** [ACTIVITIES.md](ACTIVITIES.md) documents every layer of
> heimdall's work — the doors, the gate, the degradation ladder (a higher
> rung that breaks steps down to the next and the record shows the drop), the
> executors, and the honest test/security truth.

No accounts to create for workers, no server to rent, no data ever stored on a
central server.

- **Matrix** (hyphae.social) — a room is created per fleet. The room is *only* a
  directory: it holds the members so peers can find each other and exchange
  encrypted signaling. It is not a message channel and nothing you compute ever
  lives there.
- **WebRTC** — offers/answers/ICE travel as encrypted Matrix *to-device* events
  (ephemeral, not stored in the room). Once the DataChannel is up, prompts,
  tokens, and results flow device-to-device directly.
- **WebLLM** — each worker runs a local LLM in its own browser tab via WebGPU.
  Models are cached on-device after the first download.

## Remote inference is another execution lane (2026-10)

Heimdall does not decide "call Anthropic" or "call Groq". It submits a
**HeimdallJob@1** — a description of the work, not a model name
(`schemas/heimdall-job@1.json`, `src/job.js`):","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}

Rung 5 is a donor engine, not a caller-side floor. No files edited and no processes touched. Test bridges ran on ports 18911-18914 from a scratchpad script, `floor.mjs`, in the session scratchpad dir.
  
  **Topology measured**
  - 8790 is `heimdall up --no-open`. Its upstream is **11434**, which is khora's `node proxy.mjs` (the "heimdall channel", `x-heimdall-channel: heimdall:11434`), not Ollama.

  - gemma2:2b, qwen2.5-coder:1.5b and nomic-embed are installed on Ollama. qwen2.5:14b is not.
  - So the hop chain is client → 8790 → khora channel 11434 (admission, queue, antistrauss gate) → Ollama 11435. Nothing steps down from the channel to 11435.
  
  **Floor paths**
  
  | Path | Result | Evidence |
  |---|---|---|
  | Direct 11435 `/api/chat` | PASS | 3 runs, 0.26–0.89 s, tokens returned |
  | Bridge pointed at 11435 (scratch instance), `/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` | PASS | 200 in 241–961 ms; streaming also works on all 3 stream shapes |
  | Live 8790 `/api/chat` | **FAIL (intermittent)** | 1.8 s once, 13.9 s once, and 6 timeouts at 10–40 s (000 timeouts at -m 15/-m 40) while direct Ollama was 0.3 s |
  | Live 8790 `/api/generate` | marginal | 200 in 7.2 s |
  | Live 8790 `/v1/chat/completions` | PASS | 200 in 0.65 s |
  | Live 8790 `/v1/messages` | **FAIL** | `404 {"error":"no such route on the channel: POST /v1/messages"}` (the channel serves neither this nor Anthropic wire) |
  | Dead upstream (scratch, 127.0.0.1:9) | PASS (fast, loud) | all 4 routes return 502 in 6–163 ms |
  | Missing model (scratch, 11435) | PASS | 404 in 10–170 ms, error shape native per route |
  | `--no-passthrough` | expected | 404 "not found in the fleet" |
  | Slow/hung upstream (scratch, fake server never answers) | **FAIL** | client aborted at 8 s; upstream never saw the connection close (`closed=0`), so the bridge waits forever |
  | Rung 5 in-tab WebLLM/WASM (`src/llm.js`, `src/llm-worker.js`) | **UNPROVEN** | No test. The worker and `sw.js` are served (200). Weights are not bundled, so a cold first run needs network. I did not open a tab, because that would attach a controller to the live bridge. |
  
  **Defects**
  1. **No timeout and no client-abort in `pipeUpstream`.** `src/bridge-server.mjs:701` calls `fetch()` with no `signal`. Reproduction: a hung upstream, or `curl -m 5` against the live bridge. Bridge-to-channel connections stay ESTABLISHED (7 seen, 3 after drain). Abandoned requests keep occupying the channel's single queue and delay later callers. The khora channel itself holds batch-priority requests for the queue TTL, and the bridge identifies itself as `x-er7-caller=heimdall-bridge` (line 698), which is batch priority.
  2. **No step-down from rung 4.** A 502, a channel refusal (429/403/508) or a timeout from 11434 returns straight to the caller (line 711). It never tries 11435. The `fellThrough` counter covers only fleet-to-upstream, not upstream-to-direct.
  3. **Default upstream is wrong for this machine.** `bin/heimdall.mjs:265` defaults to 11434 (the channel) when `OLLAMA_HOST` is unset, and `bridge-server.mjs:113` does the same. Real Ollama is on 11435, so the floor depends on a khora process the bridge does not own. `OLLAMA_HOST=":11435"` yields `http://:11435`, which is an invalid URL (line 265). `0.0.0.0:11435` works only because macOS connects to 0.0.0.0. A bare `11435` parses as a hostname.
  4. **`pipeUpstream` drops upstream headers** (line 708 writes only `content-type`). It loses `retry-after`, `x-queue-position` and `x-heimdall-held`, so a refused caller cannot back off. A mid-stream failure ends with a bare `res.end()` at line 712 (clean EOF, indistinguishable from completion), and `/v1/*` errors use a non-OpenAI/Anthropic shape (`{error:"string"}`).
  5. **`/v1/messages` passthrough is unsupported by the channel.** Line 910 pipes the raw body upstream. The channel's `CHANNEL_ANSWER_ROUTES` (khora `proxy.mjs`, around line 2677) omits `/v1/messages`, so the route 404s on the live setup.
  6. **Rung 5 is a donor engine, not a caller fallback.** `main.js:1775-1776` has a duplicate `if (!webgpuAvailable())` whose second branch is dead code. `WorkerEngine.infer` has no timeout or abort, so one stalled generation blocks the chained queue (`llm.js:92-97`). Concurrent `load()` calls with different model IDs race and can leak an engine (`llm.js:63-67`). `WasmEngine.load` has no in-flight guard (`llm.js:260`). A first run offline fails because weights are fetched from huggingface.co and the MLC CDN. There are no automated tests for any of it.
  7. A transient `400 Bad Request` with an empty body (Node parser, `Connection: close`) occurred 5 times on 8790 early on, then stopped. I could not reproduce it.
  
  **Smallest fixes, in order**
  1. In `pipeUpstream`, add `signal: AbortSignal.any([clientGone, AbortSignal.timeout(~120000)])`, aborting on `res.on('close')`, and forward `retry-after`, `x-queue-position` and `x-heimdall-*` headers.
  2. Add an ordered `upstreams` list `[11434 channel, 11435 Ollama]`. On 502, 429 or timeout, retry the next one when nothing has been written yet, and count it in `fellThrough`.
  3. In `heimdall.mjs`, probe 11434 for the `x-heimdall-channel` header and 11435 for `/api/version`, and warn when the channel is the floor. Normalise `:port` and bare port values of `OLLAMA_HOST`.
  4. Translate `/v1/messages` to `/v1/chat/completions` when the upstream is a channel.
  5. Add a per-infer timeout and abort in `WorkerEngine`, serialise `load()`, and remove the dead branch in `main.js`.
  
  **Defects that stop this being a guarantee:** 1, 2 and 3 (hang or stall with no fallback, depending on a non-owned proxy) and 5 (a whole wire has no floor). Defect 6 means rung 5 is unproven.

name: heimdall-embedded-peers
description: Heimdall is not a standalone daemon — every server embeds its own heimdall and the instances coordinate as peers (decided 2026-10-05)
metadata:

---

Operator decision 2026-10-05: "every server has a heimdall, and they coordinate, but there is no standalone heimdall."

**Why:** the standalone bridge (heimdall up, :8790) was the failure point — unsupervised, stale code, a browser tab as the only fleet controller, and its floor depended on khora's proxy (11434) which it did not own. Measured diagnosis in [[the-fold-pipeline-findings]] style: no timeout/abort/step-down on rung 4, frontier map cleared on a failed probe, no circuit breaker, /bridge/* unauthenticated.

**How to apply:**
- Each server (khora channel, penelope mouth, the Fold's server) mounts heimdall in-process (`createBridge` handler, no process.exit/pidfile/global state); each instance's floor (own Ollama, in-tab) works with zero peers = "possibility". Peer coordination, fleet horses, native links, frontier = "probability" layers above it.
- Low layers = possibility (always exist), high layers = probability (make the good path usual). A broken higher rung steps down; the record shows the drop.
- `heimdall/scripts/floor.sh` supervises via launchd; the bridge service there is marked `transitional` until embedding lands.
- Approved by operator the same day: restart live bridge after fixes land, launchd install, node-datachannel install, per-boot token + Host check on the gate.
"}

All five audits are in. I've redirected the running agents to your "no standalone heimdall, every server has one and they coordinate" design.

**The floor audit, the last report**

Direct Ollama is healthy, but the bridge's path to it is not a guarantee:

- **No timeout or abort on the bridge-to-upstream call.** Live `/api/chat` through 8790 timed out six times at 10–40 seconds while direct Ollama answered in 0.3 seconds. Abandoned requests keep occupying khora's single-slot queue.
- **No step-down from rung 4.** A 502, a refusal or a timeout from the channel goes straight back to the caller. Nothing tries Ollama on 11435 directly.
- **The bridge's floor isn't its own.** Its upstream is khora's proxy on 11434, which the bridge doesn't own, not Ollama on 11435.
- **`/v1/messages` returns 404** through that channel, so one whole wire has no floor.
- **Rung 5 (in-tab WebLLM) is unproven.** It has no tests and no timeout, and a cold first run needs the network.

**How the design change applies**

- **Per-server floor.** Each embedded heimdall needs its own floor, working with zero peers. That is the possibility layer.
- **Coordination layer.** Peer lending, fleet horses, native links and frontier models sit above the floor as the probability layer.
- **Agent changes.** The bridge agent now makes `createBridge` mountable (no `process.exit`, no pidfile, no globals) and does the floor fixes before the frontier and gate work. The supervision agent now has a data-driven service list, with the bridge marked "transitional."
- **Saved to memory.** The decision is recorded so later sessions don't reintroduce a standalone daemon.

**What I'm assuming**

"Servers" means khora's channel, penelope's mouth, and the Fold's own server. Peers will coordinate over loopback HTTP on one machine and over the existing Matrix swarm across machines. Tell me if that's wrong, because it shapes the peer layer.

**Next:** when the three implementers report, I'll verify their work, then build the embedded heimdall plus peer coordination, then do the restart and launchd cutover.

input: {"message":"I created `floor.sh` and `floor.test.mjs`, and all 7 tests pass (`timeout 60 node --test scripts/floor.test.mjs`). I installed, loaded and started nothing, and I did not touch the README. shellcheck is not installed, so I only ran `bash -n`.

**Files**
- `/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/scripts/floor.sh`

**Design**
- **Table:** the services are one data table at the top of the script (name, dir, runtime, args, port:health, env, transitional, optional, entry, stale-watch dirs). Rows:
  - channel (11434, 11436, 11437)

- **Install flags:** `install` takes `--dry-run`, `--without-transitional` (drops the bridge plist) and `--with-optional` (adds fold-web, off by default).
- **Secrets:** each plist runs a bash wrapper that sources `~/.heimdall/floor.env` (0600, created empty) and then `exec`s the absolute node or python3 path. No secrets are baked into plists.
- **`status`:** it reports a per-service heimdall probe (`GET <port>/heimdall/status`: "not embedded yet" on 404). The bridge prints "transitional: to be embedded into the servers above".
- **`up` guard:** `up` refuses to bootstrap a service whose port is still held by a hand-started process, because it would crash-loop.

**Real `status` (condensed)**

| service | pid | started | health | heimdall | STALE |

| channel | 98435 | 10-05 14:06 | 11434, 11436, 11437 PASS | not embedded yet | no |
| mouth | 66067 | 10-04 22:49 | 11439 PASS | not embedded yet | yes (organs/src newer, 22:52) |

**Operator decisions**
- **Inherited secrets:** the running mouth and bridge inherited `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` from opencode's shell. They are not in the plists. Decide whether they are needed and, if so, put them in `floor.env`.
- **Ollama settings:** I left `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL`, `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` and the other Ollama server settings out of the plists, since they belong to Ollama.app.
- **Channel flag:** the channel bakes in `ER7_EXTERNAL_HEIMDALL=1`, which assumes the fleet on 11438 stays up.
- **Stale-check scope:** the channel's stale check covers only `proxy.mjs`, because khora has no `src/`. I added `mouth` and `organs` for the mouth and `bin` for the bridge.

**`adopt` steps (printed only)**
1. `floor.sh install`, adding `--without-transitional` if you want to leave the bridge out. Then fill `~/.heimdall/floor.env` if the services need secrets.
2. `kill 65098` (bridge), then `kill 66067` (mouth), then `kill 98435` (channel).

4. `floor.sh status`

input: {"description":"Build peer coordination module","prompt":"You are an IMPLEMENTER. Repo: /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall. Do NOT git commit, restart/kill any process, or npm install. You own ONLY these NEW files: src/peers.js, src/peers.test.mjs, src/peers-http.js, src/peers-http.test.mjs, docs/PEERS.md. Other agents are concurrently editing src/bridge-server.mjs, remote.js, links.mjs, main.js, rtc.js, invite.js, liveness.js, route.js, swarm.js, bin/heimdall.mjs: READ them if useful (swarm.js, route.js, dispatch.js, links.mjs, README.md, ACTIVITIES.md, MULTI-SERVER.md section A) but never edit them.

DESIGN (operator decision, 2026-10-05): there is NO standalone heimdall. Every server (khora channel, penelope mouth, the Fold's server) embeds its own heimdall in-process, and the instances coordinate as PEERS. Each instance's floor (its own Ollama / in-tab engine) works with zero peers = the 'possibility' layer. Peer coordination is a 'probability' layer: it must only ever ADD options and must degrade to nothing, never become a dependency. The fleet fixes pass my own check: 37 of 37 tests, and `node --check` is clean on every `src/` file. I also ran the new liveness tests against the old HEAD `liveness.js`, and they fail there. That is a coarse red check, because the whole file fails on missing exports, not on each assertion separately. The agent had already shown 8 of 10 rtc and invite tests fail on HEAD, so those do catch the old behavior.

**What's fixed, and which symptoms it explains:**

- **Healthy horses were being dropped.** A `ready` message from a backgrounded or lease-expired horse caused the controller to drop its link, and expired horses churned about every 20 seconds. Only genuinely dead or stuck links drop now, never one with a job in flight.
- **Revocation failed open.** A failed read of the revoked list returned an empty list, and could overwrite the paired registry. It now throws, and nothing is written back from a failed read.
- **Revoked horses stayed routed.** An already-linked revoked horse is now dropped at the next tick.
- **Dead horses blocked relinking.** A broadcast to a dead horse left its in-flight flag set forever, so the tick never relinked it. There is now a 120-second deadline.
- **A transient ICE `disconnected` killed live links.** There is now an 8-second grace period.
- **Unaccepted horses were sent jobs.** A horse is routable only after it has accepted duty.
- **Room setup had no retry**, so a failed startup meant no reconcile loop until reload. It now retries with backoff.

**Heads-up from another session:** a session working on a Vertex DeepSeek lane says it's using a separate worktree on branch `vertex-deepseek`. It touches `remote.js` and `discovery.js` lightly, so a small merge overlap with the bridge agent's edits is likely. It's owner-only, off by default, and sealed-only. It needs no reply, and I won't merge it.

I'm waiting on two agents: the bridge agent (floor, frontier and gate) and the peer-coordination module. The headless-controller extraction waits behind the bridge agent, since both touch the bridge's controller endpoints.

input: {"file_path":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/docs/PEERS.md","content":"# Peers: heimdall instances that help each other, and never depend on each other

There is no standalone heimdall. Every server (khora channel, penelope mouth, the Fold's server) embeds its own
heimdall in-process. Code: `src/peers.js` (pure), `src/peers-http.js` (loopback/LAN transport).

## The model in plain words

- **Floor (possibility).** Each instance's own engine (its Ollama, its in-tab model). It works with zero peers.
  Nothing in the floor path may ever wait on a peer.
- **Peers (probability).** Other instances may be faster or hold a model this one lacks. Asking one can only ADD an
  option. A peer that is down, slow, lying or removed costs the caller at most ONE bounded timeout (`firstByteMs`),
  then a circuit breaker skips it. If no peer is eligible, `pickPeer` is `null` and the caller's floor runs unchanged.

Selection is eligibility first (privacy wall, model held, capabilities, standing, breaker), then lowest
expected time-to-accepted = (queue wait + TTFT) / success rate, success rate Laplace-smoothed (1+ok)/(2+ok+fail) as in
`route-stats.js`. A peer must also beat the caller's `floorMs` if given. Ties go to the injected `random`.

## Wire shapes

PeerHello@1 (`POST /heimdall/peers/hello`, body = sender's hello, response = receiver's hello):

    { type:"PeerHello@1", id, name, url, models:[...], caps:{tools,structured,context},
      load:{inflight,queue,tokensPerSec}, privacyClass:"local-raw"|"sealed-external",
      trustDomain?, epoch, ts }

`epoch` is per boot (an older epoch is a replay and is ignored). `ts` is never compared with our clock: standing comes from
OUR last-heard time. Lists are clipped; unknown `privacyClass` becomes `sealed-external`.

Job (`POST /heimdall/peers/infer`, body `{job}`, headers `x-heimdall-peer-token`, `x-heimdall-hops: 1`,
`x-heimdall-origin: <sender id>`): a HeimdallJob-like `{model|"any", privacy, requires:["tools"|"structured"], context?, maxTokens?, ...}`.
A job with no/unknown `privacy` is treated as `local-raw` (fails closed). Response: `200 application/x-ndjson`, one JSON chunk per
line (`{type:"delta",text}` ...), a mid-stream failure is a final `{type:"error"}` line. Before the first byte: 401 token, 403 wall/host/ban,
404 model not held, 422 caps, 429 + `Retry-After` busy, 502 floor failed, 508 loop. `GET /status` returns hello + peer list.

## Trust and the privacy wall

A `local-raw` job goes only to a peer that is (1) on OUR allowlist (`add({trusted:true})` / `setTrusted`; a hello can
never grant this), (2) declares `privacyClass:"local-raw"`, and (3) shares our `trustDomain` if either side sets one.
The lender checks the mirror image: it serves a `local-raw` job only if the origin is on ITS allowlist. So both ends must
agree. `sealed-external` jobs (projection only) may go to any peer. Discovered peers (they said hello with the token)
are untrusted and expire after `ttlMs` of silence; added peers never expire. Auth: same-machine peers share
`~/.heimdall/peers.token` (0600, created if missing); no or wrong token is 401; `Host` must be loopback or in `allowHosts`
(403). The client refuses to send the token to any other host, whatever a hello claims.

## Loop safety

A forwarded request carries hops=1 and the origin. A receiver serves it or refuses it; `pickPeer`/`run` return no peer when
`hops >= 1` and never choose the origin. The receiver rejects hops != 1 (400/508) and origin == itself (508). Two instances
whose floors both try the peer layer exchange exactly one request, never a ping-pong (`peers-http.test.mjs`).

## Failure behaviour

Standing, same bounds as `liveness.js`: unheard = `linking`; `stale` at 3 missed beats (45 s), `dead` at 6 (90 s); only
`ready` is routable; silence never removes an added peer, and a hello revives it. Breaker per peer: a timeout or auth
refusal opens at once, other errors after `f… [2281 more chars at the transcript address]

text:
The peer module is verified. All 39 tests pass on two consecutive runs of my own, and `node --check` is clean. The tests didn't write a `peers.token` into your real `~/.heimdall`.

I accept both of the agent's decisions, since both fail closed:

- **No `privacy` field means `local-raw`.** A job that doesn't say what it is can only go to a trusted peer.
- **Inbound `/infer` needs `x-heimdall-hops: 1` and an origin.** That makes a forwarded request a single hop and stops loops.

The embedder must always set `privacy` explicitly.

Fixed and verified so far: the fleet defects, peer coordination (39 tests), liveness (10 tests), and the supervision script (7 tests). Still out: the bridge agent, which is doing the floor, frontier and gate fixes. Embedding peers into the servers is the next step, and it builds on the bridge agent's mountable `createBridge`, so it waits for that report.

The bridge is rebuilt and running, with the floor, frontier and gate fixes loaded. But the "every server has a heimdall" part isn't built yet, and the channel and mouth are still hand-started. All 483 heimdall tests pass, nothing is committed, and 78 files are changed.

**What was wrong**

- **Nothing was supervised.** Every service was started by hand. The bridge was running code from about 15 hours earlier.
- **The floor had no timeouts.** The bridge's path to Ollama had no timeout, abort or step-down. Live `/api/chat` timed out six times at 10–40 seconds while Ollama itself answered in 0.3 seconds.
- **Frontier was dead.** The frontier map was cleared by one failed probe, and failing rungs were retried on every request.
- **The fleet never ran.** The only fleet controller was a browser tab, and none was open.

**What's live now**

- **Bridge supervision:** the bridge runs under launchd on 8790 and takes about 27 seconds to boot.
- **Floor:** it carries both floors, `[11434 → 11435]`, with timeouts and step-down. `/v1/messages` works, where it was a 404 before.
- **Frontier:** it is restored, with 10 providers.
- **Gate:** it refuses a spoofed Host and unauthenticated writes. Both are measured live.

**Also built and verified, not yet in use**

- **Peer coordination:** 39 tests, not wired into any server yet.
- **Fleet defects:** nine controller defects are fixed, covering dropped healthy horses, failed-open revocation and unaccepted horses being routed.
- **Supervision script:** `floor.sh`, with plists installed for all three services and only the bridge loaded.

**Mistakes I made**

- I stopped the old bridge with 8 connections open. They had appeared in the minute since my last check. Whatever was calling it lost those requests. After that I only restarted when the connection count was 0.
- A startup probe could permanently drop the direct-Ollama fallback. I found and fixed it, test-first.
- A test that depended on the live channel hung for 123 seconds, and two others needed a gate token. All three are fixed, and the test bridges no longer reach the live channel.
- I only saw the `bridge-khora` failure once and couldn't reproduce it.

**Needs your attention**

- **Fold key entry:** the Fold's provider-key entry now needs a one-time visit to the bridge page (for the cookie) or `heimdall key` in a terminal. The Fold's `/api/code` calls work through the origin allowlist.
- **Commit risk:** the working tree depends on untracked modules, so committing only the modified files would crash the committed bridge on import. They need to be committed together.

**Not done**

- **Channel and mouth cutover:** both are still hand-started, because evals are using them. Run `floor.sh adopt` when the evals are idle, or tell me to.
- **Embedding:** mounting heimdall plus the peer handler inside khora's proxy, penelope's mouth and the Fold's server.
- **Headless controller:** it needs an `npm install` of node-datachannel, which you approved.

Should the next step be the embedding or the channel and mouth cutover? The embedding means editing khora's and penelope's server files, which other sessions may be changing.
